main_body: stone tower building with conical green roof
top_band: green tiled conical roof slope from row 4 to row 40 (with gold finial at rows 0-3)
evidence: The building has a clearly visible upper roof surface (rows 4-40) above the vertical stone wall face (rows 41-95). At the roof edge (rows 39-42) there is a distinct dark eave and brown trim overhanging the stone wall, and the window (rows 50-63) and doorway (rows 68-91) are recessed with inner frames and shadows.

style.evidence: Compared to the Beodeul reference buildings on the left, the stone wall is made of large repetitive flat grey blocks (around 6x3 px of flat fill per brick) lacking the fine per-stone speckle, varied stone sizes, and rich 5-6 step contrast of house-h112_0-stone. The roof tiles are simple checkerboard-like blocks rather than individually highlighted scalloped tiles, and the door/window are very flat and geometric.
